valuation.conventions: P/B (or P/ABV where NPAs distort book) read against RoE - the P/B-vs-RoE regression IS the sector's valuation map; sustainable RoE above cost of equity mechanically justifies >1x book. Peer within model class only: large private != SFB != PSU. Never use EV multiples or EBITDA language.

overlays.business_model: Sector model: spread business on a levered balance sheet - the P&L IS the balance sheet. Growth without asset quality is future credit cost. Franchise quality = liability side (CASA, granular retail deposits) more than asset side. Revenue quality ladder: granular retail NII > fee income (recurring) > treasury gains (cyclical) > one-off recoveries.
overlays.financials: Replace industrial D1/D2/D3 entirely. Analyze: (1) RoA tree - NII/assets + fees/assets - opex/assets (cost-income) - credit cost/assets -> RoA; x leverage -> RoE; name the moving lever. (2) NIM decomposition: yield on advances vs cost of funds; floating books reprice with repo, deposits lag ~2-3 quarters -> NIM expands in hiking cycles, compresses in cuts; separate mix effect from rate effect. (3) Growth quality: WHERE the book grows (unsecured personal/MFI = high-yield high-risk; secured mortgage = slow safe) - segment mix shift IS the risk story. (4) Asset quality full set: GNPA/NNPA + slippages (leading) + credit cost + PCR + write-off-adjusted view + restructured book. (5) Capital: CET1 vs growth plans. Counter-cyclical provision buffers = management prudence signal.
overlays.supply_chain: Reframe entirely: a bank's supply chain is its FUNDING (deposits: granularity, bulk dependence, top-20 depositor share, CASA stickiness) and its DISTRIBUTION (branch/digital mix, DSA dependence for origination, co-lending partners). Concentration lens: depositor concentration, sector concentration of the loan book, top-20 borrower share.
overlays.governance: Sector-typical: divergence reports (RBI-assessed vs disclosed NPAs - any divergence is an automatic red flag); promoter/group exposure of the book; evergreening signatures (restructured accounts regrowing, fresh lending to stressed groups' SPVs); management tenure vs RBI approval cycles; auditor comments on IT/controls.
overlays.peers: Peer within model class. NIM comparisons require similar book mix - a 6% NIM MFI-heavy book is not 'better' than a 4% mortgage book, it is differently risky. Always pair growth with asset-quality columns - growth alone misleads.
overlays.risks: Sector signatures: credit cycle position by segment (unsecured retail, MFI stress cycles); deposit-funding strain (CD ratio, bulk dependence); NIM compression in rate-cut cycles; regulatory actions (PCA, business restrictions, divergence); concentration (borrower, sector, depositor); ALM for anything wholesale-funded; technology/UPI disruption of fee pools.
overlays.industry: Cadence: RBI fortnightly credit/deposit data; monthly business updates (many banks pre-release); quarterly results with slippage detail; RBI policy (repo + stance + liquidity); FSR twice yearly. System credit growth vs nominal GDP is the demand anchor.
overlays.valuation: Frame P/B against sustainable RoA/RoE from the tree, not headline. State where the bank sits on the sector's P/B-vs-RoE line and whether the deviation is explained by asset-quality or growth-mix differences.
overlays.takeaways: Monitorables vocabulary: next quarterly slippage number, monthly business update growth split, RBI policy dates, FSR commentary on the bank's dominant segments, deposit growth vs credit growth gap.

forensic_signatures: GNPA improvement driven by write-offs while credit cost stays elevated
RBI divergence in NPA recognition (any amount)
Fee income from upfront-booked assignment/securitization gains
Deposit growth concentrated in bulk/certificates while CASA bleeds
Lending to promoter-adjacent or stressed-group entities
classic_mistakes: Using EBITDA, FCF, or working-capital language for a lender
Reading high NIM as quality without the risk mix
Judging asset quality on GNPA alone while write-offs do the cleaning
Comparing SFB/MFI economics to large private banks
Missing that credit growth is future credit cost when underwriting slips
